title: First instruments: piano, violin and a homemade banjo
summary: He disliked piano and violin, built a stringed instrument from a seagull box, and Coochie Martin's guitar strings; the kitchen trio.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: My sister, one of my sisters attempted to learn the piano when she was in high school. And, uh, she completed one or two grades, but she didn't follow it through. And then I started on the piano. When was your first instrument? That was my first instrument. About how old were you?
About seven or eight years old.

That's right. And, uh, I didn't like the piano. I didn't like that because at that time, uh, they had things that was called your music role. Oh yeah. It'd fold up. And sometimes it was made out of plush and different colors like that. And they passed down from my sister to me her music role that she had to take her music book in. And, uh, the fellas would kid me and call me a sister. I didn't like that. So I just continued playing, uh, the violin. So many girls played piano.
That's what I heard too. That a lot of boys, they thought it would be all sisters.

Yeah, and the violin. Uh, that's the first instrument that my father wanted me to learn. My mother wanted me to learn the violin. But, uh, I didn't like the violin. The first instrument that I had, I made, it was out of a seagull box.

It was made out of a seagull box and in the manual training room at school I made a neck and made the pegs to put in it. And, uh, a friend of my father's name, Mr. Coochie Martin, he was a guitar player. Oh yeah.
So he was one of the family of the Martins?

One was a drummer and the other one was the... That was the Henry Martin that was a drummer. That's right. Well, the one that they called Coochie Martin. Whenever he would break one of his guitar strings my dad would bring it home to me.

And, uh, use it on a little shirt. And I would, uh, tune it up and, uh, not with the proper tuning, I would just tune it up to my imagination, what sounded like a chord to me. Yeah. And would strum without the finger, just move my fingers from one place to another across the bar, you know. And, uh, I sang, in fact my sisters and I sang, we sing nicely together. Uh, we had what was called a kitchen trio in the afternoons when the dishes were being washed we used to sing. Uh, uh, my father would appreciate our singing and told us that we sang very well. Uh, getting back to the instrument.
